answer: Proof-of-stake bonding turns each identity into a collateralized bet, so a sybil swarm must fund every node before acting. An agent stakes tokens that vest over time and are slashed if peers reject its work, making each fake identity a costly liability rather than a free asset. To flood the vote, an attacker needs the full bond on ten thousand wallets and pays the slashing penalty when validators catch the pattern across the ocean of duplicates. Reputation accrues only on aged, verified agents, so a fresh raven cannot mimic a long ridge of honest history.
